models_evaluated: pretrained convolutional neural network for femoral condyle alignment classification

links.outcome: Radiographer accept/reject performance with versus without AI annotations; overreliance on incorrect AI
links.effect: Sensitivity identical with and without AI (0.64); no significant differences in specificity, PPV, NPV; inter-reader agreement lower with AI (AC 0.233 vs 0.374); false AI feedback reduced sensitivity and specificity in repeated cases.
links.quote: Radiographers' sensitivity was identical with and without AI support (0.64), with no significant differences in specificity, PPV, or NPV.

links.outcome: Susceptibility of radiographers to incorrect AI advice (automation bias)
links.effect: False AI feedback reduced sensitivity and specificity in repeated cases, indicating susceptibility to incorrect AI advice.
links.quote: False AI feedback reduced sensitivity and specificity in repeated cases, indicating susceptibility to incorrect AI advice.

links.outcome: Human-AI team performance versus unaided readers in the workflow
links.effect: AI feedback did not improve overall performance (sensitivity 0.64 in both arms) and lowered inter-reader agreement (AC 0.233 vs 0.374).
links.quote: AI feedback did not improve overall performance in assessing lateral knee positioning and may reduce consistency, particularly among users without AI experience.
